newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea opposition says willing to talk over new law.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea opposition says willing to talk over new law.

text.p: South Korea's main opposition party said on Friday it was willing to hold talks in parliament over a controversial new labour law if the government apologised for its forced passage, a party spokesman said.
The National Congress for New Politics had previously said it and a smaller opposition party would only hold dialogue with the government if the legislation was first revoked.
"If the government apologises for ramming the law through parliament we are willing to start talks over the law," Park Hong-yeop, deputy spokesman for the National Congress, told Reuters.

"We will interpret an apology as returning to square one, although the government would probably see it as only revising the law. We will leave that to the Korean people to judge." Park said his party expected the apology to come from the speaker of the National Assembly.

On Wednesday, the National Congress and the United Liberal Democratic Party rejected an offer by President Kim Young-sam to reopen debate in parliament over the law, which had sparked more than three weeks of wildcat stoppages.
The ruling New Korea Party rammed the bill through parliament during a dawn session on December 26 while opposition deputies slept.
